blocks.text: 我们发布 PARDIG 和 SatWeave，帮助研究人员和开发者构建新的天气、水文和气候应用。

inlines.text: 我们发布 PARDIG 和 SatWeave，帮助研究人员和开发者构建新的天气、水文和气候应用。

blocks.text: 要理解和预测地球的天气与水循环，首先取决于我们当下能多好地观测地球。卫星和地面仪器持续、细致地监测着这颗星球。但要把这些原始测量数据转化为一幅连贯的全球图景并快速提供出来，是一项重大的科学与工程挑战。

inlines.text: 要理解和预测地球的天气与水循环，首先取决于我们当下能多好地观测地球。卫星和地面仪器持续、细致地监测着这颗星球。但要把这些原始测量数据转化为一幅连贯的全球图景并快速提供出来，是一项重大的科学与工程挑战。

blocks.text: 今天，我们发布两个基础数据集 SatWeave 和 PARDIG，支持全球社区构建天气、水文和气候应用。这两个数据集对我们近期发布的 WeatherNext 3 模型的进步至关重要。SatWeave 是地球静止卫星影像的全球拼图，为模型提供发展中的云和风暴的实时视图。PARDIG 是一个基于 AI 的全球降水数据集，用于训练该模型的降水预报。我们同时提供这两个数据集的历史存档和实时数据流，方便研究人员和开发者在建模及下游应用中使用。

blocks.text: SatWeave：来自太空的地球统一视图

inlines.text: SatWeave：来自太空的地球统一视图

blocks.text: SatWeave 整合了五颗卫星的影像，它们覆盖全球不同区域：GOES-East 和 GOES-West、Meteosat 0 和 Meteosat Indian Ocean，以及 Himawari。由于各卫星使用不同的地图投影、文件格式、传感器和扫描时间表（间隔从 10 到 30 分钟不等），要形成一幅连贯的全球地图并不容易。现有的大多数全球合成产品会舍弃不兼容的部分，只提供四个或更少的通道，或者每隔几小时才更新一次。

inlines.text: SatWeave 整合了五颗卫星的影像，它们覆盖全球不同区域：GOES-East 和 GOES-West、Meteosat 0 和 Meteosat Indian Ocean，以及 Himawari。由于各卫星使用不同的地图投影、文件格式、传感器和扫描时间表（间隔从 10 到 30 分钟不等），要形成一幅连贯的全球地图并不容易。现有的大多数全球合成产品会舍弃不兼容的部分，只提供四个或更少的通道，或者每隔几小时才更新一次。

blocks.text: SatWeave 将六颗地球静止卫星的观测融合成一幅全球拼图，涵盖 17 个可见光、水汽和红外通道。

blocks.text: PARDIG：全球范围内准确的高分辨率降水

inlines.text: PARDIG：全球范围内准确的高分辨率降水

blocks.text: 降水影响着从粮食和水供应到洪涝与干旱风险的一切，但要在全球范围内准确追踪降水仍是一大挑战。地面雷达和密集的雨量计网络能提供高质量数据，但并非所有地区都有这些设施，或覆盖良好。

inlines.text: 降水影响着从粮食和水供应到洪涝与干旱风险的一切，但要在全球范围内准确追踪降水仍是一大挑战。地面雷达和密集的雨量计网络能提供高质量数据，但并非所有地区都有这些设施，或覆盖良好。

blocks.text: 为帮助弥合这一差距，我们开发了 PARDIG（降水 AI 再分析：密集推断 GPM）。PARDIG 采用与 WeatherNext 3 类似的 AI 架构，直接以 NASA 全球降水测量（GPM）核心观测站稀疏的星载雷达观测为训练数据，并以 SatWeave 影像和 ECMWF 的大气场作为输入。最终得到一幅高度准确的全球降水图，时间分辨率为 15 分钟，空间分辨率约为 10 公里，平均延迟约五小时更新。

inlines.text: 2025 年 7 月得克萨斯丘陵地区山洪暴发期间的逐小时降雨，对比了基于地面的 NOAA MRMS 雷达（左，约 1 公里）、近实时的 PARDIG（中，约 10 公里）和 IMERG-Final（右，约 10 公里）。

blocks.text: 我们针对美国、欧洲和日本的三大大陆雷达网络，以及全球超过 36,000 个气象站，对 PARDIG 进行了评估。在所有分析的降雨强度下，PARDIG 均优于全球领先的基线模型，包括 NASA 的 IMERG-Final——这是一个研究级降水估算数据集，对无数应用至关重要。在轻至中度降水上，PARDIG 的逐小时降水检测能力比 IMERG-Final 提升超过 30%。它在捕捉极端降水方面尤其有效，而现有全球产品往往难以检测到这类降水。

blocks.text: We are releasing PARDIG and SatWeave to help researchers and developers build new weather, hydrology, and climate applications.

inlines.text: We are releasing PARDIG and SatWeave to help researchers and developers build new weather, hydrology, and climate applications.

blocks.text: Understanding and predicting the planet’s weather and water cycle starts with how well we can observe the Earth right now. Satellites and ground instruments monitor the planet continuously and in great detail. But converting these raw measurements into a coherent global picture and making it available quickly, is a major scientific and engineering challenge.

inlines.text: Understanding and predicting the planet’s weather and water cycle starts with how well we can observe the Earth right now. Satellites and ground instruments monitor the planet continuously and in great detail. But converting these raw measurements into a coherent global picture and making it available quickly, is a major scientific and engineering challenge.

blocks.text: Today, we are releasing two foundational datasets, SatWeave and PARDIG, to support the global community in building weather, hydrology, and climate applications. Both datasets are key to the advances in our recently released WeatherNext 3 model. SatWeave is a global mosaic of geostationary satellite imagery that provides the model a live view of developing clouds and storms. PARDIG is an AI-based global precipitation dataset that was used to train the model’s precipitation forecasts. We are making historical archives and live feeds of both datasets available, so researchers and developers can use them in their modeling and downstream applications.

blocks.text: SatWeave: A unified view of Earth from space

inlines.text: SatWeave: A unified view of Earth from space

blocks.text: SatWeave combines imagery from five satellites, which cover different parts of the globe: GOES-East and GOES-West, Meteosat 0 and Meteosat Indian Ocean, and Himawari. Because each uses different map projections, file formats, sensors, and scan schedules (ranging from 10 to 30 minutes), it is difficult to form a coherent global map. Most existing global composites drop incompatible aspects, offering only four or fewer channels, or updating every few hours.

blocks.text: SatWeave blends observations from six geostationary satellites into a global mosaic across 17 visible, water vapor, and infrared channels.

blocks.text: SatWeave updates hourly and thus allows WeatherNext 3 to produce new global predictions, in contrast to models initialized on analysis data refreshed every six hours. We are releasing this hourly live feed, and a historical archive spanning over a decade.

blocks.text: PARDIG: Accurate, high-resolution precipitation across the globe

inlines.text: PARDIG: Accurate, high-resolution precipitation across the globe

blocks.text: Precipitation shapes everything from our food and water supplies to the risk of floods and droughts, yet tracking it accurately across the planet remains a major challenge. While ground radars and dense rain gauge networks provide high-quality data, they aren't always available or have good coverage in all regions.

inlines.text: Precipitation shapes everything from our food and water supplies to the risk of floods and droughts, yet tracking it accurately across the planet remains a major challenge. While ground radars and dense rain gauge networks provide high-quality data, they aren't always available or have good coverage in all regions.

blocks.text: To help bridge this gap, we developed PARDIG (Precipitation AI Reanalysis: Densely Inferred GPM). Built on an AI architecture similar to WeatherNext 3, PARDIG is trained directly on sparse spaceborne radar observations from the NASA Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Core Observatory, using SatWeave imagery and atmospheric fields from ECMWF as inputs. The result is a highly accurate global precipitation map at 15-minute temporal resolution and roughly 10-kilometer resolution, updated with an average latency of about five hours.

blocks.text: We have performed evaluations of PARDIG against three continental radar networks across the US, Europe, and Japan, as well as over 36,000 weather stations worldwide. PARDIG outperforms leading global baselines across all analyzed rain rates, including NASA’s IMERG-Final, a research-quality dataset of precipitation estimates that is incredibly important for countless applications. PARDIG improves hourly precipitation detection skill over IMERG-Final by more than 30% on light-to-moderate precipitation. It proved particularly effective at capturing extreme precipitation, which can be challenging for existing global products to detect.

blocks.text: Because PARDIG learns directly from satellites rather than relying solely on ground-based measurements, we expect it to have reliable accuracy everywhere on Earth, even in areas where these measurements are not available.

blocks.text: Along with the live data feed, we are releasing historical archives of PARDIG data from 1999 to 2026. While WeatherNext 3 used PARDIG for medium-range weather forecasting, we're excited to partner with, and enable, the community in exploring improved models for floods, landslides, and drought, especially in regions without dense ground radar networks.

As the latest addition to Google’s Earth AI portfolio, we hope these datasets empower researchers around the world to open new ways of connecting weather observations to crucial, real-world applications.
